comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of credit spreads on fair value of loans
comparisons.peer_summary: The estimated net loss from changes in instrument-specific credit spreads on loans and lending commitments under the fair value option was $125 million in 2023 and $281 million in 2022, but was not material for 2024. The firm calculates fair value by discounting future cash flows using rates that incorporate these credit spreads, with floating-rate instruments driven primarily by spread changes and fixed-rate instruments also affected by interest rate changes.
comparisons.comparison: Both C (target) and GS disclose the financial impact of instrument-specific credit spread changes on liabilities/loans where the fair value option is elected. C reported a significant loss of $573 million in 2024 due to changes in its own credit spread on non-derivative liabilities, whereas GS reported that the loss from such changes on loans and lending commitments was 'not material' for 2024, contrasting with previous years where losses were $125 million (2023) and $281 million (2022). Both disclosures explain that fair value calculations incorporate instrument-specific credit spreads.

sentences.text: The estimated changes in the fair value of these non-derivative liabilities due to such changes in the Company's own credit spread (or instrument-specific credit risk) were a loss of $573 million and a loss of $2,078 million for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

The estimated net loss attributable to changes in instrument-specific credit spreads on loans and lending commitments for which the fair value option was elected was not material for 2024, $125 million for 2023 and $281 million for 2022.

The firm generally calculates the fair value of loans and lending commitments for which the fair value option is elected by discounting future cash flows at a rate which incorporates the instrument-specific credit spreads.
